## Overview

This model is a fine-tuned version of **ByT5-small** for processing transliterated Akkadian texts.
Thanks to byte-level tokenization, it handles rare characters, diacritics, and orthographic variation typical of ancient Near Eastern corpora.

The model is designed for research in digital humanities and Akkadian NLP.

---

## Training Data

Fine-tuning was performed on transliterated Akkadian texts collected from:

* **SEAL – Sources of Early Akkadian Literature** ([https://seal.huji.ac.il/](https://seal.huji.ac.il/)) 
* Data provided through the **Deep Past Challenge (Kaggle)**

A processed, web-scraped subset of the training data is available here:

👉 **Dataset (partial):** https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/xjoannax88/akkadianenglish-lexical-index 

Note: The shared dataset represents only part of the full training corpus. Some web-collected materials are not redistributed.
---

## Intended Use

Suitable for:

* Text normalization
* Sequence-to-sequence tasks
* Experimental Akkadian language modeling
* Digital humanities workflows

---

## License

Released under the **MIT License**.

Users are responsible for ensuring appropriate attribution and compliance with any applicable rights associated with the original data sources.

instances.overview:
Fine-tuned ByT5-small model for processing transliterated Akkadian texts.
Optimized for byte-level sequence-to-sequence tasks such as normalization, transformation, and experimental language modeling in digital humanities workflows.
instances.usage:
```python

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM

model_name = "xjoannax88/akkadian-byt5"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_pretrained(model_name)

# --- Word-level translation ---
prompt_word = (
    "Translate Akkadian to English. Dictionary entry.\n"
    "Akkadian: šarrum"
)

inputs = tokenizer(prompt_word, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=64)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))


# --- Sentence-level translation ---
prompt_sentence = (
    "Translate Akkadian to English. Sentence.\n"
    "Akkadian: šarrum ana ēkallim illik"
)

inputs = tokenizer(prompt_sentence, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=128)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))

```

# Enhanced Audio Anomaly Detection

A production-ready machine learning system for detecting anomalies in industrial machine audio (e.g. fans, pumps, sliders, valves, toy cars/conveyors) using a hybrid ensemble of pretrained transformer embeddings (Audio Spectrogram Transformer) and classical signal processing features.

Trained and evaluated on the **DCASE 2020 Task 2** dataset.

### Best Results
- **Pump**: 0.874 AUC (GMM-16 on hybrid features) – +5.9% over sklearn baseline
- **Average AUC across 6 machines**: 0.753 (hybrid) vs. 0.773 (classical baseline)

See full results table in the README.

### Key Features
- 1723-dimensional hybrid features: 768-dim AST embeddings + 955 classical features (MFCCs, spectral stats, temporal descriptors)
- Multiple detectors: GMM, OCSVM, XGBoost, Isolation Forest, LOF, Elliptic Envelope
- Production-ready: inference scripts, model persistence, comprehensive logging
- Unsupervised options for anomaly detection on normal-only data
- Detailed visualizations: ROC curves, confusion matrices, feature importance

### Intended Use
- Industrial predictive maintenance
- Anomaly detection in noisy environments
- Benchmarking on DCASE-style tasks

### Limitations
- Domain-specific: Best on machine sounds similar to DCASE 2020
- Requires labeled normal/anomalous data for supervised methods
- Classical features dominate on some machines; AST helps semantics but has domain mismatch

### How to Use
See **Example Usage** below or publish an example notebook for quick start.

Full documentation, code, and experiments:  
GitHub → https://github.com/or4k2l/enhanced-audio-anomaly-detection

instances.overview:
This is a fine-tuned variant of the MIT Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) pretrained on AudioSet.  
We added 955 classical audio features (MFCCs, spectral stats, etc.) to create 1723-dim hybrid features,  
and trained an ensemble (GMM, OCSVM, XGBoost) for improved performance on industrial machine sounds (DCASE 2020 Task 2).
Best result: 0.874 AUC on Pump.

It includes:

models.provenanceSources:
This model is a custom hybrid audio anomaly detection system developed from scratch, incorporating a fine-tuned version of the **Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST)** pretrained backbone.

**Pretrained backbone**:
- Model: Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) fine-tuned on AudioSet (equivalent to ViT applied on spectrograms)
- Original source: MIT CSAIL (paper: AST: Audio Spectrogram Transformer, arXiv:2104.01778)
- Pretrained checkpoint reference: MIT/ast-finetuned-audioset-10-10-0.4593 (originally from Hugging Face Transformers library)
- License of pretrained component: BSD-3-Clause

**Training data**:
- Dataset: DCASE 2020 Task 2 – Unsupervised Anomalous Sound Detection for Industrial Machines
- Source: Official DCASE challenge website
- Link: https://dcase.community/challenge2020/task-unsupervised-detection-of-anomalous-sounds
- Only normal machine sounds were used for unsupervised training methods; labeled data used for supervised evaluation and benchmarking.

**Additional components developed by the creator**:
- Classical audio features (955 dimensions): extracted using librosa (MFCCs, spectral statistics, temporal descriptors)
- Hybrid feature fusion: Concatenation of AST embeddings (768-dim) + classical features → 1723-dim vectors
- Ensemble detectors: GMM, One-Class SVM, XGBoost, Isolation Forest, LOF, Elliptic Envelope trained on the hybrid features
- No private, proprietary, or external user-uploaded data was used beyond the public DCASE dataset.

**Reproducibility**:
- All training, evaluation, and inference scripts are provided in the GitHub repository.
- Repository: https://github.com/or4k2l/enhanced-audio-anomaly-detection
- License: MIT (entire custom model and code)

The model was fully developed, trained, and evaluated by the creator (orecord / Yahya Akbay) in 2025/2026 using only publicly available resources and datasets.
models.subtitle: Hybrid AST + Classical Features for Industrial Audio Anomaly Detection – DCASE 2020 Task 2 (0.874 AUC on Pump)

# MediQA-Qwen2.5-0.5B-Chat

## Model Details

`
- Model Name: MediQA-Qwen2.5-0.5B-Chat
- Base Model: Qwen2.5-0.5B
- Fine-Tuning Method: LoRA (PEFT)
- Task: Medical Question Answering (Multiple Choice)
- Language: English
- Framework: PyTorch + Hugging Face Transformers
`

MediQA-Qwen2.5-0.5B-Chat is a parameter-efficient fine-tuned medical QA model built on the Qwen2.5-0.5B causal language model. The model is adapted using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to specialize in medical multiple-choice reasoning tasks.
This release contains LoRA adapter weights only (not a merged full model).

## Base Model
The model is built on:
- Qwen Qwen2.5-0.5B
- Transformer decoder-only architecture
- ~0.5B parameters

## Dataset:
`dataset = load_dataset("lavita/medical-qa-datasets", "med-qa-en-4options-source")`
